hazards_worth_recording: **A SLOPE SCAN THAT RANKS THE LOUDEST AXIS RANKS THE ONE THE FEET CANNOT SEE.** v1 of `f10-r7a-slope-scan.mjs` sampled a symmetric cross on both axes and took the maximum. Its top pick scored **0.6811 m**; `--probe-only` stood the player there and the bones read **0.0258 m**. All of that 0.68 m ran north-south and **the feet are separated east-west**. The scan was measuring a real feature of the terrain that the effect under test is blind to, and it would have sent the Pod to photograph a fourth consecutive null — the exact failure it was written to end, one level up. Fixed by taking the foot offsets from a live probe (`foot_l` +0.1003/-0.056, `foot_r` -0.1003/-0.064) and ranking on the ground difference BETWEEN THE BONES. The model then reproduced all three live readings to within 1 mm.

**AN OFFLINE RE-IMPLEMENTATION OF A DERIVATION IS A SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH, AND IT DRIFTED IMMEDIATELY.** `f10-r7a-shotlist.mjs` re-derives `characterFor()`'s hash from `actor.js`'s own source rather than retyping the pools, which is the careful version — and it still disagreed with the running game on **4 of 4** subjects. The capture is unaffected because it reads `userData.actor.characterId` out of the live scene. The lesson is the ordering: a planning model is allowed to be a RANKER (which stand, roughly which people) and must never be the ANSWER, and anything it predicts must be re-read from the thing itself before it is spent on.

**MY OWN THREE NEW TOOLS ALL RAN THEIR WHOLE CLI ON IMPORT, AND ONE OF THEM DID IT TO ME.** A one-line `import()` written to check the foot model against three probe readings kicked off a 1,442,401-point scan and printed its table before the check ran. That is HAZARDS §16's third defect — *'importing `f10-r3-materials.mjs` runs its entire capture and exits'* — reproduced by an agent who had read the entry that morning. All three now carry `IS_CLI`. **`tools/visual/f10-r6-appearance-compare.mjs` had the same hole and it was live**: importing its two statistics ran round 6's entire comparison and `process.exit()`ed out of the importer. It is guarded now, which is what makes `f10-r7-appearance-read.mjs` able to import them instead of copying them.

**`node --check` AND A SELF-TEST DO NOT TELL YOU THE CAMERA IS POINTED AT A WALL.** Every tool here passes a self-test with arms required to disagree — 11, 10, 7, 5 checks — and the wide slot still came back at 0.176%. The only instrument that would have caught it is a cheap local frame, and the first version of this capture DID produce one: a SwiftShader smoke run showed an empty plaza, which is why the anchor moved from an offline centroid to the live scene. It moved to the right kind of anchor and still not close enough. **A geometry self-test proves the camera is where you asked; only a picture proves you asked for the right place.**

**`--probe-only` PAID FOR ITSELF TWICE IN ONE AFTERNOON AND COSTS NOTHING.** A mode that runs every scene READER against the live game and takes no screenshots finishes in ~3 minutes on SwiftShader where a full capture is ~45 s per frame. It found the wrong-axis slope stands and confirmed the replacements before a Pod existed. Its first run was killed by its own timeout and left NOTHING on disk although the crowd census had already completed; the write is now in a `finally`, which is HAZARDS §13's 'land what you have' applied to a measurement instead of a fix.
